response: {"text":"The paper describes a theoretical construct consisting of a wheel‑like assembly of magnetic elements whose like poles line the outer rim while the opposite poles are gathered at the centre. When a fast electron travels along the axis toward this assembly, it can set the whole structure into rotation, creating a circulating magnetic effect. If the electron’s incoming speed is below a certain critical value, the interaction is perfectly elastic: the electron bounces back without losing energy, and the point where its direction reverses may lie on either side of the wheel’s plane, depending on its initial speed. If the speed exceeds that limit, the electron penetrates the structure, emerges slower, having transferred a fixed quantum of energy to the rotating wheel. In the elastic case the wheel’s spin is cancelled when the electron returns; in the inelastic case the wheel retains its spin, and the stored rotational energy later appears as emitted radiation."}
